Let me play Scion of Draco for 2 mana first (gives trample, so even blocking is futile), then attack.

annotations.description: Playing Mountain as the land drop limits future mana options. With Scion of Draco in hand (which costs 2 less per basic land type), maximizing domain is important. Playing Godless Shrine (paying 2 life) would add Plains and Swamp types, giving 3 basic land types with the opponent's Overgrown Tomb already covering Swamp/Forest. Then cracking the battlefield Arid Mesa for a Mountain would give 4 types (Plains, Swamp, Mountain, Forest), making Scion of Draco cost only 4. Playing Mountain first means the Mesa can only find Mountain or Plains - getting Plains gives Mountain+Plains (2 types from own lands). With Godless Shrine played instead, cracking Mesa for Mountain gives Plains+Swamp+Mountain = 3 types from own lands, better domain. The Mountain can always be played later, but Godless Shrine untapped costs life that's better paid now when at 20.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Mountain from hand as the land drop for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Godless Shrine (paying 2 life to have it enter untapped) to get Plains and Swamp types. Then crack Arid Mesa for a basic Mountain to get 3 basic land types immediately, setting up a cheaper Scion of Draco and enabling Territorial Kavu as a 3/3 next turn if a green source is found.

annotations.description: Phlage was cast from hand, not escaped. When Phlage enters without escaping, its triggered ability forces you to sacrifice it. The ETB trigger will deal 3 damage and gain 3 life, but then Phlage immediately gets sacrificed. This wastes the card entirely as a 3-mana Lightning Helix that goes to the graveyard. While Phlage in the graveyard enables future escape, spending 3 mana and a card for just 3 damage/3 life when you have Teferi, Time Raveler and Scion of Draco in hand is very poor. Teferi could bounce the opponent's Dredger's Insight (disrupting their graveyard strategy which fuels Yawgmoth combos) while drawing a card, and its static ability would prevent the opponent from casting at instant speed. The opponent is on a Yawgmoth combo deck and Teferi's static shuts down many of their lines.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury from hand for {1}{R}{W}, which will be immediately sacrificed since it didn't escape.
annotations.betterLine: Crack Arid Mesa for a fetchable land if needed, then cast Teferi, Time Raveler ({1}{W}{U} using Temple Garden, Godless Shrine, and finding an Island or using existing lands). Teferi's -3 could bounce Dredger's Insight and draw a card, while the static ability prevents opponent from using instant-speed abilities. If blue mana isn't available, at minimum save Phlage for escape later and use Arid Mesa to fix mana for Teferi or Scion of Draco on a future turn.

annotations.description: At 2 life, the opponent has Phlage in their graveyard with exactly enough mana (RRWW from Mountain, Steam Vents, Temple Garden, Godless Shrine) and exactly 5 other cards in graveyard to escape Phlage next turn for lethal 3 damage. Agatha's Soul Cauldron can exile Phlage from the graveyard with its tap ability, preventing this lethal threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Dredger's Insight, which mills cards and provides incremental value but does nothing to prevent the opponent from escaping Phlage for lethal damage next turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Agatha's Soul Cauldron for {2}, then tap it to exile Phlage from the opponent's graveyard, removing the lethal escape threat. Could also play the Forest first for additional mana flexibility.

annotations.description: At 4 life facing two ~5/5 Territorial Kavus, the player needs to assemble the Yawgmoth combo immediately. Agatha's Soul Cauldron is the key piece: next turn, tap Cauldron to exile Walking Ballista from graveyard (putting a +1/+1 counter on Young Wolf), then cast Yawgmoth with 4 mana from lands. This enables the infinite combo: sacrifice Young Wolf to Yawgmoth, it returns with undying +1/+1 counter, remove the counter to ping (Ballista ability from Cauldron), repeat for infinite damage. Badgermole Cub doesn't meaningfully help survive against two 5/5s and delays the combo by a critical turn.
